fact_text: The analyst's case for OGDC rested on trade debts not rising over two quarters after the IMF deal, which suggested reported profits were being received as cash.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: OGDC was described as Pakistan's largest oil producer with multiple fields, and its crude sales to refineries are larger than PPL's, which the analyst saw as lowering its circular-debt exposure.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For upstream gas producers, circular debt absorbs much of reported profit: in the analyst's example only about 20 to 30% of profit was received in cash, while the rest built up as trade debts.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A quick quarterly check is whether trade debts grew by less than cash profit; if receivables grow more slowly than profit, the circular-debt risk is under control.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IMF programmes put heavy focus on circular debt, so the analyst treats circular-debt control as the first variable to check for oil and gas producers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Royalty and windfall levies are deducted from oil producers' revenue, so the realised price per barrel is well below the international oil price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To estimate an oil discovery's EPS effect, multiply daily output by about 330 producing days and the realised price per barrel, take about a 35% net margin, then divide by shares outstanding.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The EPS effect of a discovery is turned into a fair-value effect by multiplying it by the P/E ratio, which the analyst applied because long-life reserves keep producing for many years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For an upstream producer, EPS moves almost in line with the realised oil price, so the analyst valued such companies on EPS at a normalised oil price rather than the spot price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Domestic oil discoveries reduce the amount of crude that must be imported, which lowers the country's oil import bill.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The KSE-100 is a total-return index that already includes dividends, so comparing it with rent must subtract the assumed dividend yield to avoid double counting.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani equity earnings have historically doubled about every four years, roughly 18% a year by the rule of 72; net of a 4-5% dividend, this leaves about 13% a year from capital growth.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Dividends come out of profit, so a company's dividend tends to grow at about the same pace as its profit over time, in the analyst's view.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Property rent typically grows slowly, while index dividends grow with profits, so over long horizons index dividends can overtake rent, in the analyst's example.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Property returns are reduced by maintenance, occasional long vacancies and rent-collection problems, which headline rental-yield comparisons with index dividends often leave out.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Holding a market index spreads exposure across many businesses, so the investor does not need to identify which single company will lead in future, which lowers concentration risk.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stocks vs Property: Which Will Make You Richer in Pakistan?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
